The nomination signals are shared Grade ancestry, weak local rank proximity (rank_gap 0), and token/trigram overlap on generic items ('comprehension', 'questions', 'the', 'would'), none of which establishes developmental support. There is nevertheless genuine instructional coherence beyond generic repetition: both skills develop higher-order, inferential question-answering about narrative text, one in shared reading and one in oral listening, so they are complementary reinforcing skills across strands. relatesTo (symmetric, null direction) is therefore the correct canonical judgment. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the identical resolved coordinate scope (Grade R, rank 0, Term 2, Listening and Speaking (Oral), sub-strand 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning', same source table row/page), so direction cannot rest on rank or term order and must come from substantive content. The source texts and Learning Components show a pair-specific increase in demand: 'Looks carefully at pictures and talks about common experiences' (LCs: 'Looks carefully at pictures'; 'Talks about common experiences') is single-image close observation plus talk tied to familiar experience, whereas 'Orders a sequence of pictures and relates the story created' (LCs: 'Sequences pictures'; 'Relates the story created from the ordered pictures') requires attending to several pictures, imposing a temporal order, and orally constructing a connected narrative. Direction is lower-to-higher rank (Grade R to Grade 1), matching the only permitted buildsTowards direction; the shared 'posters' token alone was not treated as sufficient, the pair-specific shift in cognitive demand is. They are substantively coherent reading skills — self-monitoring of word recognition and comprehension is the strategic behaviour exercised while reading continuous text, and independent reading of picture/story books is the setting in which such monitoring is applied — so the pair shows meaningful mutual reinforcement within the same term's reading programme. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Emergent Writing / Emergent Handwriting Skill statements (coordinate rank 0, Grade R). The first is Term 1 ('Uses a range of writing tools: paint brushes, wax crayons etc. during free indoor play or creative art activities'); the second is Term 3 ('Begins to form letters: uses finger painting, paint brushes, wax crayons, pegboards or elastic boards'). Comfort and control with the tools in Term 1 supports success in forming letters in Term 3, so buildsTowards runs first_to_second. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit under Grade 1 (rank 1), so direction must be fixed by Term. The second SFI ('Begins to use capital letters and full stops, including capital letters for names') is Grade 1 / Term 3 / Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing; the first SFI ('Uses terms such as sentence, capital letter, full stop') is Grade 1 / Term 4 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / Daily-Weekly activities. Term 3 to Term 4 is the only permitted developmental direction within the grade. The substantive change is not mere repeated wording: the Term 3 statement is practical application of capitalisation and end punctuation in the learner's own writing, while the Term 4 statement requires the learner to name and talk about those same conventions using the metalanguage 'sentence, capital letter, full stop'. Hands-on use of capitals and full stops in writing plausibly supports the later oral use of that terminology, which is a support relationship rather than a strict prerequisite. Confidence is moderate because the two statements sit in different Skill Areas and both SFIs' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), so the full printed context could not be inspected.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R Skill statements concerning early perceptual-motor laterality/directionality: the first (Term 3, EMERGENT READING > Emergent reading skills) is 'Develops eye movements. For example, follows a pencil moved from left to right'; the second (Term 1, EMERGENT WRITING > Emergent Handwriting) is 'Crosses the midline: takes the right hand across the midline to touch the left shoulder etc.' Their LC tags ('eye movements', 'left to right', 'tracking' vs 'gross motor', 'handwriting', 'midline') show complementary left/right and midline-crossing foundations that reinforce each other across reading and writing readiness, which is substantive coherence beyond the weak shared-ancestor (Grade R) and low token overlap (jaccard ~0.14 on 'left', 'right', 'to') signals. However, the supplied CAPS text does not state that gross-motor midline crossing is a support for visual left-to-right tracking; the two sit in different Skill Areas and sub-strands with no stated dependency, so an earlier-Term-to-later-Term buildsTowards (second_to_first) would rest on inference rather than this bounded evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

The first SFI (Grade R, Term 3, Emergent Handwriting) is 'Begins to form letters: uses finger painting, paint brushes, wax crayons, pegboards or elastic boards' — the same letter-formation goal executed with fine-motor media and tools. Shared LC tags (letter formation, handwriting, motor) plus the Term 2 -> Term 3 ordering within the same grade indicate substantive deepening from large-muscle, kinaesthetic letter shaping to tool-mediated emergent letter formation, so proficiency in the Term 2 skill supports success in the Term 3 skill. Direction is second_to_first (earlier Term to later Term), which is the only permitted developmental direction here; the reverse would be an invalid later-to-earlier Term link. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R (rank 0) but in different terms: the second ('Arranges a set of three pictures ... form a story and a logical sequence of events when verbalised and relates the story created') is Term 1 under Listening and Speaking (Oral), sub-strand 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning', while the first ('Interprets pictures to make up own story: ‘reads’ the pictures') is Term 2 under Emergent Reading, sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills'. Direction is therefore constrained to the permitted earlier-to-later Term order (second_to_first). The pair is not mere repeated wording: the Term 1 skill has the learner construct and verbalise a narrative from a supplied, scaffolded set of three pictures (sequencing LC tags 'sequencing', 'logical order', plus 'relates the story created'), whereas the Term 2 skill asks the learner to independently interpret pictures as if reading them to generate their own story within the emergent-reading strand. Competence in deriving and telling a coherent story from a picture sequence plausibly supports success in independently 'reading' pictures to make up an own story, so a developmental support relation from the Term 1 oral picture-sequencing skill to the Term 2 emergent-reading skill is the best-supported permitted judgment. Note that source evidence for both endpoints and LC evidence for the first endpoint are truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts, identity scopes and LC claims shown; this limits certainty but does not make the evidence contradictory.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 1, Term 4 (rank 1, same term), but in different Skill Areas: the second is 'Uses consonant blends to build up and break down words' under Reading and Phonics / Daily Phonic Activities (LC tags: blending, building words, consonant blends, segmenting), while the first is 'Spells common words correctly' under Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing (LC tags: spelling, common words, writing). Phonic blending and segmenting of words with consonant blends (sp-o-t, st-i-ck) is the decoding/encoding capability that underpins accurate written spelling of words, so proficiency in the phonics skill supports success in the writing-spelling skill; the reverse direction is not similarly supported. Direction is same-Term within Grade 1, which the Term ordering rule permits. Judged on word-level sound-to-letter coherence, not on the weak shared token 'words' or shared Term/Grade ancestry alone; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, so confidence is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R Emergent Writing (rank 0) and both concern a child contributing to a shared class text, so they are substantively coherent rather than merely sharing a parent grade. Source scope evidence places the second SFI in Term 1 ('Contributes ideas for a class news book by means of drawings') and the first in Term 4 ('Contributes sentences to a class piece of writing: child dictates as the teacher writes'). The within-grade change is substantive rather than repeated wording: contributing via drawings is the earlier, non-verbal mode of contributing content, whereas dictating full sentences for the teacher to scribe requires composing oral sentence-level language that is transcribed into print. Proficiency in contributing ideas to a class text by drawing supports success in contributing dictated sentences, so the permitted direction runs from the earlier Term 1 skill (second) to the later Term 4 skill (first). Source-evidence and LC truncation flags limit the excerpts but the term, skill-area and statement texts supplied are consistent and unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 3, Skill Area WRITING, but under different sub-strands: 'Handwriting' ('Copies and writes at least two letters of joined script or cursive writing per week (size and uniformity)') and 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' ('Spells common words correctly and attempts to spell unfamiliar words using phonic knowledge'). They are complementary transcription components of written recording — letter formation/legibility on one side (LCs tagged copying, cursive, handwriting, letters) and orthographic/phonic encoding on the other (LCs tagged spelling, common words, phonic knowledge) — so they cohere substantively within the same term's writing work. Neither statement's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other: cursive letter formation does not develop spelling accuracy, and spelling with phonic knowledge does not develop joined-script handwriting; the only overlaps supplied are the token 'and', weak trigram/page/rank proximity and the broad 'writing' LC tag, which cannot establish developmental direction. Same Grade and same Term also provide no ordering evidence. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading Skills, but they sit in different sub-strands and address different capacities: the first (Term 1, 'Begins to make meaning of written text') is a concepts-of-print/print-awareness statement that written words correspond to spoken words, while the second (Term 4, 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness') is oral identification of rhyming words in rhymes, songs and rhyming sequences. The Term 1 to Term 4 ordering would permit a forward developmental direction, but the evidence shows no substantive dependency: rhyme detection is an auditory/oral skill that does not require the print-to-speech mapping insight, and neither statement extends, deepens or broadens the other. The shared token 'words' and the shared Grade R ancestor are not themselves semantic support. They remain complementary foundations of the same Grade R emergent-reading programme, which supports symmetric conceptual coherence rather than buildsTowards. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), but the full statement text and identity scope are present and unambiguous for this judgment.

They cohere substantively as complementary exposure to and handling of a widening range of text types (graphical/visual texts versus genre texts such as play scripts) within the same term's reading programme, so each meaningfully reinforces the other's breadth-of-text-type goal. However, neither statement's capability is a plausible support for success in the other: interpreting charts and advertisements does not specifically enable reading play scripts, nor the reverse, and both sit at the same grade rank and the same Term 3, giving no evidence of an earlier-to-later developmental step. Shared LC token overlap is limited to the generic tag 'reading' and filler tokens ('as', 'such'), which alone cannot support a developmental direction. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment; endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), but the printed statements and identity scopes are complete enough for this conclusion.

Earlier Term to later Term within the same grade is a permitted developmental direction, so buildsTowards runs second_to_first. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 2 Writing Skills under the same 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' sub-strand: 'Uses present, past and future tenses correctly' (Term 3) and 'Begins to spell common words correctly' (Term 2). They are complementary written-language conventions applied in the same independent-writing context (LC tags: grammar/tenses/writing vs spelling/common words/writing), giving substantive conceptual coherence. However, accurate spelling of common words does not specifically support or enable correct tense usage (nor vice versa); they are parallel, distinct conventions, so no developmental dependency is warranted even though the Term 2 to Term 3 direction would be permitted. The only lexical overlap ('correctly', shared trigrams) is generic. Endpoint source evidence is truncated and multiple ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, but the available statement text and term/skill-area placement are unambiguous for this symmetric judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are distinct printed bullets in the same Grade 1, Term 1, Reading and Phonics table row under the sub-strand 'Emergent reading skills', with identical resolved coordinate (Grade 1, rank 1) and identical ancestor path. Semantically they are complementary emergent whole-word/environmental-print recognition skills: 'Recognises own name and names of at least ten peers' and 'Reads labels and captions in the classroom' both involve sight recognition of familiar printed words in the immediate classroom environment, so they reinforce each other in instruction. The evidence shows no substantive expansion of capability (no increase in text length, letter knowledge, or independence) and no sequencing between the two co-listed Term 1 bullets, so a same-rank, same-term developmental direction is not supported; the overlap flagged by nomination (shared ancestors, same page 60, token 'and', shared LC tag 'reading') is weak and would not alone establish a relation, but the shared emergent-print-recognition content is substantive enough for symmetric coherence. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits confidence but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills are printed bullets in the same Grade 1 / Term 4 / WRITING table row under the sub-strand 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' (page 81, window 25), at the identical Grade coordinate (rank 1) and identical Term. The first — 'Contributes ideas for and helps to revise a class/group story (Shared Writing)', with LCs for contributing ideas and helping to revise collectively — and the second — 'Writes and illustrates sentences on a topic to contribute to a book for the reading corner', with LCs for writing and for illustrating sentences on a topic — are complementary composing activities: collective idea generation/revision supports and is reinforced by learners producing their own sentences for a class book. This is substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence rather than generic repetition (the statements share no distinctive content wording; token/trigram overlap is dominated by stopwords, and the only shared LC tag is the broad token 'writing'). It is not, however, sufficient for a same-rank, same-Term developmental claim: the two bullets are parallel Term 4 items in distinct activity modes (collective oral contribution and revision of a class story vs. independent written-and-illustrated product), and the shared-to-independent gradient is read from the sub-strand label and shared parentage, which are hierarchy signals that cannot alone establish buildsTowards. Canonical relatesTo with null direction is therefore the supported judgment. Material limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge/code context (including merged Grade and Term banner nodes), so the full printed context is not visible.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the same Grade 3 (rank 3), Term 2, READING AND PHONICS table, but under different printed sub-strands: 'Paired/Independent Reading' ('Reads own and others' writing') versus 'Shared Reading' ('Reads enlarged texts such as poems, big books, posters and electronic texts as a whole class with the teacher'). They are complementary components of the same term's reading programme - teacher-led whole-class reading of enlarged published texts alongside learner-autonomous reading of self- and peer-authored writing - which is substantive conceptual coherence in reading practice. The bounded evidence does not show that proficiency in one specifically supports success in the other: the texts, grouping and purposes differ (published enlarged texts with teacher mediation vs. peer/own writing read independently), and same-Term co-placement plus shared LC tokens ('reading', 'texts', 'reads') and page proximity are not developmental evidence. relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment rather than either buildsTowards direction. Source evidence and LC evidence for the endpoints are truncated, limiting finer discrimination.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R, Term 1, Skill Area 'Emergent Reading' (rank 0, same term), but under different printed sub-strands: 'Emergent reading skills' (first: completing a visual picture, e.g. puzzles — a visual-perception readiness activity, LC tags 'visual perception', 'puzzles') and 'Shared Reading' (second: 'reading' enlarged texts such as poems, big books and posters as a whole class with the teacher). They are complementary components of the same emergent-literacy programme rather than one conferring capability on the other: puzzle/picture completion is a visual-discrimination activity, while shared reading is a teacher-led whole-class text experience, and nothing in the bounded evidence shows the one being an expansion or precondition of the other. Same-term, same-grade placement with only generic token overlap ('a', 'as', 'such') and the broad shared LC tag 'reading' does not supply the substantive evidence required for a same-rank developmental direction, so the symmetric relation is the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is flagged truncated (24 omitted items each), so the reading is based on the bounded excerpts.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 2, Term 3 Skills but sit in different Skill Areas and sub-strands: the first is a WRITING / Handwriting bullet ('Copies and writes short words in joined script or cursive writing: 2 and 3 letter words such as an; am; at; it; in; on...'), the second is a READING AND PHONICS / Daily Phonic Activities bullet ('Reads words from phonics lessons in sentences and other texts'). The shared word-level focus is substantive rather than merely lexical: the handwriting list consists of exactly the kind of short phonically regular words and sight words encountered in phonics lessons, so decoding/reading those words and forming them in cursive reinforce each other within the same term's programme. However, the evidence shows no dependency: handwriting fluency in joined script is a motor/transcription demand that neither requires nor is required by reading phonic words in connected sentences, and within the same Grade and same Term there is no sequencing evidence to justify a developmental direction either way. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Note the shared Term 3 / Grade 2 ancestors are merged banner nodes and both endpoints' source evidence (and the second endpoint's LC evidence) is truncated, so only the bounded excerpts above were used.
